A score that represents the sentiment of the given document, trained on headlines providing short commentary and editorials on global equity markets. Scores can take values of -1, 0, or 1 indicating negative, neutral, or positive sentiment, respectively. This sentiment score is based on RavenPack's Expert Consensus Methodology.

A granular score between -1.00 and +1.00 with up to 2 decimal places that represents the sentiment of a given document by combining various sentiment analysis techniques. The direction of the score is determined by looking at emotionally charged words and phrases and by matching documents typically rated by experts as having short-term positive or negative share price impact. The strength of the score (values above or below 0, where 0 represents neutral strength) is determined from intraday stock price reactions modeled empirically using tick data from approximately 100 large cap stocks.

A score that represents the sentiment of the given document, trained on headlines about corporate action announcements. Scores can take values of -1, 0, or 1 indicating negative,neutral, or positive sentiment, respectively. This sentiment score is based on RavenPack's Expert Consensus Methodology and has been trained on stories that lead up to a pre-identified corporate action announcement.

"A score between -1.00 and +1.00 that measures how the event affects the creditworthiness of the entity.  A positive credit sentiment score indicates a high possibility of the entity paying back its debt; a negative score means the event signals the entity may have trouble paying back its debt. A score of 0 indicates the event has a neutral impact on the creditworthiness of the entity or simply not applicable. "

A score between -1.00 and +1.00 that represents the sentiment for the document by analyzing the language in each and every sentence. The score is calculated by averaging the sentiment across all sentences in the document.

A granular score from 0.00 to +1.00 with up to 2 decimal places, that provides a measure of the confidence when determining the DOCUMENT_SENTIMENT. This confidence score is measured from the same aggregated sentiment distribution used to compute the DOCUMENT_SENTIMENT. A value under 0.20 indicates very low confidence and a value above 0.80 reflects very high confidence.

A positive integer value that represents the entity’s level in an organizational hierarchy. A value of 1 indicates that the entity sits at the top of the hierarchy. For example, a value of 1 would be assigned to a parent or holding company which may own one more units or subsidiaries. A value of 2 indicates that the entity is a child of a parent entity, 3 indicates it’s a -grandchild, and so forth.

An integer score between 0-100 that indicates how strongly related the mention of an entity is to the underlying document, with higher values indicating greater relevance. A score of 0 means the entity was passively mentioned while a score of 100 means the entity was prominent in the document.

A score between -1.00 and +1.00 that represents the story-level sentiment for a given entity by combining the analysis of the language in each and every sentence where the entity is mentioned, with event sentiment detected for the entity across the document.

A granular score from 0.00 to +1.00 with up to 2 decimal places, that provides a measure of the confidence when determining the ENTITY_SENTIMENT. This confidence score is measured from the same aggregated sentiment distribution used to compute the ENTITY_SENTIMENT. A value under 0.20 indicates very low confidence and a value above 0.80 reflects very high confidence.

A score between -1.00 and +1.00 that represents the text-level sentiment for a given entity by analyzing the language in each and every sentence where the entity is mentioned. The score is calculated by aggregating sentiment probability distributions (the output of the ML model) for these sentences and then taking the mean of the final sentiment probability distribution. The aggregation is a weighted average where the weights correspond to the confidence scores for each of the underlying sentences.

A granular score from 0.00 to +1.00 with up to 2 decimal places, that provides a measure of the confidence when determining the ENTITY_TEXT_SENTIMENT. This confidence score is measured from the same aggregated sentiment distribution used to compute the ENTITY_TEXT_SENTIMENT. A value under 0.20 indicates very low confidence and a value above 0.80 reflects very high confidence.

A positive integer value from 0, where 0 means that the entity was directly detected in the event or it was inferred from an entity directly detected in the event (such as from a known product ownership relationship); 1 means that the entity was indirectly detected through a unit match; 2 means that the entity was indirectly detected through the match of a unit of a unit; and so forth. The score measures the distance between a parent and its units or subsidiaries.

"An integer between 0-100 that reflects the relevance of the event in the document. An event relevance score is assigned for records relating to an event, where related records can be identified by having the same EVENT_SIMILARITY_KEY within a story. The score is based on the earliest mention and frequency of the event match, according to the table below. The score is incremented for additional mentions of the event in the same paragraph, up to the maximum score for that paragraph. First in Title or Headline 100 Subsequent in Title or Headline 90-99 Paragraphs 1 & 2 80-89 Rest of document 0-79"

A positive float value between 0 and 1.00 that measures the possibility that the event will negatively affect the entity. The higher the score, the greater the risk. Values closer to 1 indicate a higher probability for loss and no opportunity for gain. Values closer to 0 mean the risk probability of the event causing loss or damage is lower. A value equal to 0 means the event presents no risk for the entity or the risk is unknown.

A score between -1.00 and +1.00 that represents the sentiment for a given entity playing a role in an event. The score is determined by systematically matching documents typically categorized by financial experts as having short-term positive or negative financial or economic impact.

A granular number with up to 5 decimal places which indicates the number of days since a document with a similar event was detected over the last 365 days. Values range between 0.00000 and 365 inclusive. A value of 365 means that the most recent document with a similar event may have occurred 365 or more days in the past. The value 0.00000 means a document with a similar event occurred at the exact same timestamp.

A score between -1.00 and +1.00 that measures how the event (and the role played by the entity) is likely to impact their country's or regional interest rates. The score refers to the benchmark interest rate set by central banks only only. A positive score indicates the event carries a dovish sentiment and is more likely to support expansionary monetary policy, including low interest rates. A negative score indicates the event has a hawkish sentiment and is more likely to favor "tight" monetary policy, including higher interest rates. A score of 0 means the event will have a neutral impact on the benchmark interest rate set by the central bank where the entity operates.

A combined score that represents the sentiment based on the tone of the document, trained on documents that mention companies with high relevance. scores are positive (1) and neutral (0) or negative (-1) and neutral (0). Entities with a relevance of less than 90 will always have a neutral score. The Erlanger Volume Swing (EVS) index is a ratio between up and down volume. In the EVS, the total volume for a given day is divided into two portions according to the position of the close between the day's true high - the higher of today's high and yesterday's low - and the true low - the lower of today's low and yesterday's high. True high and true low eliminate the problem of limit days and more suitably distribute volume on gap days. The separate up volume and down volume are then smoothed exponentially.

The Volume Swing (EVS) index is a ratio between up and down volume. In the EVS, the total volume for a given day is divided into two portions according to the position of the close between the day's true high - the higher of today's high and yesterday's low - and the true low - the lower of today's low and yesterday's high. True high and true low eliminate the problem of limit days and more suitably distribute volume on gap days. The separate up volume and down volume are then smoothed exponentially.
